summary: Independent GRAVEYARD expectations/execution pass covered all 12 active-batch companies. Current market values show that strong operating evidence is already paired with very elevated expectations in much of the batch. This lane does not assign or alter Earth Score and does not create official Action States before T0. Where consensus or defensible per-share scenarios are not reproducible from current primary evidence, they remain unknown. Highest expectation risk appears in ARM, RKLB, ALAB, ANET, AMD and CRDO; MU is uniquely exposed to cyclicality after a historic earnings/margin surge despite a lower headline multiple on current earnings.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: At roughly $37.9B market cap versus $234M Q2 revenue, the market is pricing years of launch/space-systems growth and successful Neutron execution. Current operating momentum is strong but valuation leaves little room for program failure.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Neutron schedule/capex, launch failures, contract timing and backlog conversion.
unknowns: Defensible 3-5 year diluted share count and normalized free-cash-flow margin.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Execution remains strong enough to grow into valuation without material dilution or schedule slippage.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~$30.6B market cap against ~$1.59B TTM revenue implies a very high sales multiple despite rapid profitability. The valuation assumes hyperscaler concentration remains an accelerator rather than a cliff risk.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Top-customer program changes and next earnings/customer-mix disclosure.
unknowns: Independent consensus revisions and normalized end-customer duration economics.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Revenue diversifies materially while high growth and gross margins persist.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~$50.3B market cap versus $392.4M Q2 revenue puts substantial weight on Scorpio becoming a major product family and continued >AI-market growth. High gross margins support quality but do not neutralize ramp risk.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Scorpio production ramp and Q3 revenue guide conversion.
unknowns: Current customer concentration and defensible long-run operating margin after portfolio expansion.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Scorpio ramp broadens customer base and sustains growth while operating leverage remains strong.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: A ~$5.27T market cap embeds extraordinary durability of AI infrastructure spend, platform share and margins. Primary evidence still supports exceptional demand, but customer concentration, export controls and internal/custom accelerators make the expectation bar unusually high.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: China/export policy, next architecture transition, hyperscaler capex and gross-margin trajectory.
unknowns: Reproducible long-run consensus terminal margin and custom-accelerator displacement assumptions.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: NVIDIA sustains platform share and monetization while broadening enterprise/sovereign demand beyond a few CSPs.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~$838B market cap and triple-digit trailing P/E imply a strong assumption that data-center accelerator growth and CPU share gains persist. Q2 data-center growth supports the narrative, but valuation requires continued execution against NVIDIA and custom silicon.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Instinct roadmap adoption, export controls and next major hyperscaler deployments.
unknowns: Durable accelerator gross margin and independent customer breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AMD converts current design wins into broad repeat accelerator deployments with expanding operating margin.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~$1.73T value is large but supported by exceptional current FCF and AI custom-silicon/networking growth. Relative to faster-growth peers, current forward multiple is less extreme, though concentration in a few hyperscaler programs and financed megaprojects remains material.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Custom-accelerator customer wins/losses, VMware integration and debt/capital returns.
unknowns: Customer-specific AI economics and long-run growth after current megaproject ramp.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI customer diversification and recurring software cash flow sustain growth while leverage falls.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~$1.98T value reflects both leading-edge monopoly-like economics and geopolitical resilience expectations. Relative to current revenue scale, valuation is high but less extreme than several design-layer peers; Taiwan risk is not captured by ordinary earnings multiples.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Taiwan geopolitics, overseas-fab cost, advanced-node capex and customer mix.
unknowns: Market-implied geopolitical risk premium and normalized overseas-fab margin drag.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Geographic diversification scales without major margin dilution and leading-node share remains dominant.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~54x trailing earnings prices substantial persistence of EUV scarcity and AI-led wafer-fab expansion. Backlog supports visibility, but export policy and customer capex cycles create asymmetric downside if orders normalize.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: October earnings, China restrictions and High-NA adoption economics.
unknowns: Current 2026 geographic revenue mix and customer-level High-NA utilization.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: High-NA adoption accelerates with strong service attach and backlog remains resilient through capex normalization.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ARM has the clearest valuation-expectation mismatch risk in the batch: ~259x trailing and >100x forward earnings alongside top-five customer concentration of ~57%. The market is pricing a major expansion of royalty economics into AI/data center/physical AI.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Data-center CSS adoption, Arm China economics, SoftBank-related arrangements and RISC-V substitution.
unknowns: How much future server/AI economics are already contracted versus aspirational ecosystem TAM.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Royalty mix and CSS licensing compound substantially faster than current revenue while concentration declines.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Headline forward multiple looks inexpensive because current HBM/memory earnings are extraordinary. Execution risk is not overvaluation in the ordinary sense; it is peak-cycle normalization risk. A low forward P/E can be misleading if scarcity margins are not durable.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Sep. 30 earnings, HBM4 qualification/share, capex expansion and memory ASP trajectory.
unknowns: Normalized mid-cycle HBM/DRAM margins after industry supply response.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Strategic customer agreements and HBM technology lead keep margins structurally above historical memory-cycle norms.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~60x trailing earnings requires AI-networking growth and exceptional margins to persist. The balance sheet and software-led operating model support quality, but cloud-titan concentration makes current valuation sensitive to a common AI-capex reset.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Cloud-titan budgets, 1.6T product adoption and competitive fabric shifts.
unknowns: Current top-customer revenue shares and independent customer breadth of AI deployments.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI-networking wins diversify beyond current cloud leaders while margins stay near present levels.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ~$95.5B value after ~99% one-year market-cap growth reflects belief that AI power/cooling scarcity converts into durable high-margin backlog. The key execution question is conversion quality rather than raw order growth.
perCompanyCoverage.eventRisk: Backlog conversion, hyperscaler build delays, tariffs and power/interconnection constraints.
unknowns: Current TTM revenue/margin normalized on a comparable basis and backlog cancellation terms.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Backlog converts on schedule with sustained price-cost and broad customer mix.

materialFindings.finding: ARM carries the highest plainly observable expectation burden in the batch on current market data, with ~259x trailing and ~106x forward P/E while its filing reports ~57% revenue concentration in the top five customers.

RKLB, ALAB, CRDO, ANET and AMD also require aggressive continuation assumptions relative to current revenue/earnings scale; strong business truth does not automatically imply attractive execution timing.
MU's low forward P/E is potentially deceptive because fiscal-Q3 margins/revenue are historically extreme; normalized mid-cycle earnings matter more than headline forward valuation.

Broadcom currently combines very high absolute valuation with unusually strong cash generation, making its expectation risk more dependent on custom-AI customer concentration and project durability than on a simple trailing multiple.

contradictions: High Earth-quality evidence and strong operating growth coexist with elevated market expectations across much of the batch; neither should overwrite the other.
Low forward P/E in MU does not necessarily mean low risk because current earnings may be near a scarcity-cycle extreme.
unknowns: No official pre-T0 Action State or Execution Score should be published from these observations.
Analyst consensus values from secondary market pages were not treated as canonical evidence.
Defensible bear/base/bull per-share values require normalized diluted-share counts, cash/debt and long-run margins from company-underwriting dossiers and remain unknown here.

peerRequests.request: Provide normalized diluted-share counts, cash/debt and mid-cycle margin assumptions for each batch company before any per-share valuation bands are built.
Carry customer-concentration and shared AI-capex downside into any later opportunity assessment rather than treating each ticker as independent diversification.
Test which batch companies retain economics in an AI-capex slowdown versus merely participating in the same spending wave.

accuracyDebates.reason: Especially important for MU; forward P/E can fall as cyclical earnings peak.
Prevents market data from silently creating rank/action authority before methodology-1.0 dossiers are complete.
